186.question: Under a plurality (relative majority) system, the winner is the candidate who...

options.A: Received more votes than each rival
options.B: Necessarily received more than half of all votes
options.C: Heads the list of the largest party
options.D: Represents the district with the highest turnout
options.E: Received at least two thirds of the votes

187.question: The condition for winning under an absolute majority system is...

options.A: Any lead over the nearest rival
options.B: At least half of the votes counted
options.C: More than half of the votes counted
options.D: At least one third of the votes counted
options.E: The largest number of first and second preferences

188.question: Three candidates received 46%, 34% and 20% of the votes. What is the result under a plurality system?

options.A: The election is automatically declared invalid
options.B: The seat is divided among the three candidates
options.C: The candidate with 34% is elected as a compromise
options.D: A second round between the two leaders is mandatory
options.E: The candidate with 46% is elected

189.question: Under an absolute-majority requirement, the candidates received 49%, 32% and 19%; there are no other conditions for winning and no special rules. It follows that...

options.A: The third candidate's votes automatically transfer to the first
options.B: The candidate with 32% receives a compensatory seat
options.C: No candidate has yet met the condition for election
options.D: The candidate with 49% is already elected
options.E: The seat is divided in proportion to the votes

190.question: The defining principle of a proportional electoral system is...

options.A: Distributing seats by the area of territories
options.B: The mandatory receipt by each deputy of an absolute majority
options.C: The victory of one candidate in each district
options.D: The distribution of seats in accordance with the votes for lists
options.E: The transfer of seats in proportion to the number of party leaders

191.question: The advantage usually associated with the single-member majoritarian system is...

options.A: The result's independence from district boundaries
options.B: An exact match between the shares of votes and seats for all parties
options.C: A more direct link between the deputy and the voters of the district
options.D: Guaranteed representation of every small party
options.E: A mandatory multiparty governing coalition

192.question: Why can a party win more districts while receiving fewer votes nationwide?

options.A: Because the national count replaces the district results
options.B: Because of the automatic transfer of the losers' votes to the winner
options.C: Because of differences in the territorial distribution of support
options.D: Because of the mandatory proportional compensation of all votes
options.E: Because each vote has a different weight set in advance by law

193.question: The deliberate alteration of district boundaries to obtain a favorable party result is called...

options.A: Legitimation
options.B: Absenteeism
options.C: Panachage
options.D: Gerrymandering
options.E: Co-optation

194.question: In a hypothetical single nationwide district, 100 seats are distributed with no threshold and no rounding. The lists received 40%, 35% and 25%. The number of seats the second list receives is...

195.question: An electoral threshold is introduced primarily in order to...

options.A: Ensure the exact representation of every small group
options.B: Eliminate all party coalitions
options.C: Replace voting with the appointment of deputies
options.D: Limit excessive fragmentation of the representative body
options.E: Increase the number of independent candidates

196.question: In a hypothetical system with 100 seats, a 5% threshold and votes of 50%, 30%, 16% and 4%, seats are divided proportionally only among the parties that cleared the threshold. The second party's share of seats before rounding is...

options.A: 33.33% of the seats
options.B: 31.25% of the seats
options.C: 34% of the seats
options.D: 30% of the seats
options.E: 28.8% of the seats

197.question: Under a closed (rigid) party list, the order in which seats are awarded is determined by...

options.A: The decision of the voters of an individual single-member district
options.B: The age of the candidates after the votes are counted
options.C: The order of candidates established in the list
options.D: The number of personal preferences for each candidate
options.E: A draw among all the candidates

198.question: Under a free (open) list in the typology described, the distribution of seats among candidates depends on...

options.A: A fixed position set in advance by the party apparatus
options.B: The individual preferences of the voters
options.C: The area of the candidate's home territory
options.D: Each candidate's length of party membership
options.E: The mandatory advantage of the head of the list alone

199.question: A semi-closed list is distinguished from a free one by...

options.A: The guaranteed receipt of a seat by the candidate at the top of the list
options.B: The distribution of seats only by lot
options.C: A ban on expressing preferences for other candidates
options.D: The absence of voting for a party list
options.E: The mandatory election of all candidates on the list

200.question: A mixed electoral system combines elements of...

options.A: Guild and nomenklatura selection
options.B: Federation and confederation
options.C: Majoritarian and proportional systems
options.D: Direct and hereditary rule
options.E: Traditional and charismatic legitimacy

201.question: In the described points-based model of consensus choice, the voter...

options.A: Votes exclusively against everyone
options.B: Marks only one candidate
options.C: Transfers the vote to the winner of the first round
options.D: Ranks all the candidates by preference
options.E: Chooses only a party program without candidates

202.question: In a hypothetical points-based model, five candidates receive 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1 points for first through fifth place. A candidate was ranked 1st, 3rd and 5th by three voters. His total is...

options.A: 8 points
options.B: 10 points
options.C: 12 points
options.D: 9 points
options.E: 11 points

203.question: Indicate the actions that are part of the electoral process.

options.A: Compiling a public rating of the personal authority of future deputies
options.B: Nomination and registration of candidates
options.C: Election campaigning
options.D: Agreeing on the appointment of deputies with the incumbent party leaders
options.E: Voting and tabulation of results

204.question: Conditions that ensure the democratic character of the organization of elections:

options.A: Registration of candidates conditional on the executive branch approving their programs
options.B: Impartial election management bodies
options.C: Review of complaints by the very body whose decisions are being appealed, without independent oversight
options.D: Non-discriminatory voter registration
options.E: Independent adjudication of electoral disputes

205.question: All parties are allowed to nominate candidates, but only one has access to the main channels of campaigning. Which condition has been violated?

options.A: The requirement of the territorial organization of the state
options.B: A fair distribution of election campaign resources
options.C: The principle of hereditary legitimacy
options.D: The principle of two-stage voting
options.E: The right to a mandatory absolute majority

206.question: Risks associated with the majoritarian system:

options.A: Vulnerability to manipulation of district boundaries
options.B: A weakening of the deputy's orientation to the local interests of the district
options.C: More accurate proportional representation of small parties nationwide
options.D: Distortion of the ratio of votes to seats
options.E: A reduction in the importance of the territorial concentration of party support

options.E: The seats of each candidate on the list are determined independently of the list model adopted

208.question: The campaign stage in the described sequence begins after...

options.A: The dissolution of the election commissions
options.B: The announcement of the final results
options.C: The formation of the new government
options.D: The registration of candidates
options.E: The deputies' assumption of office

209.question: Observation is necessary after voting has ended as well because...

options.A: Voting is automatically canceled after the polling stations close
options.B: The observers themselves distribute the seats at their discretion
options.C: Voters are obliged to disclose their choice publicly
options.D: Observation replaces the legal procedure for counting votes
options.E: Falsification is possible during the counting and transmission of results

210.question: Correct correspondences between a rule and a system:

options.A: Distribution of seats in accordance with votes for lists: proportional
options.B: Distribution of seats in proportion to the number of district victories: list proportional
options.C: Winning with the largest number of votes in a district: plurality
options.D: A combination of district and list election: mixed
options.E: A fixed order of the candidates on a party list: majoritarian
